title: Finite adic sections on an arbitrary affine open

from.place: finite-level hypotheses before the algebraic limit argument

statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I an ideal sheaf, F a coherent formal I-module, and V an affine open. Set T_n=F_n(V), with index n representing positive level n+1. Each T_n is a finite module over Γ(X,V), is annihilated by I(V)^(n+1), and the successor section transition T_(n+1) → T_n is surjective with kernel I(V)^(n+1)T_(n+1). Only finite levels and successor maps occur; no inverse limit property is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 087W, first proof paragraph, and Lemma 087X (2); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087X checked 2026-10-13

proof.text: Coherence implies quasi-coherence and finite type on the locally Noetherian scheme X. Apply the proved affine finite-section helper in the finite-type affine criterion to each level on V.

The affine ideal-product theorem supplies quasi-coherence and the section range of each positive ideal power. Its proved multiplication_range helper identifies the power-product inclusion range with I(V)^(n+1) times the module sections. At level n the inclusion has zero source, hence zero range, giving annihilation.

The proved product_qc helper gives quasi-coherence of the power product. Apply the affine cokernel-image theorem to its inclusion into level n+1: the quotient projection is surjective and has kernel the inclusion range. The defining formal quotient isomorphism conjugates this projection to the successor section map. Its section linear equivalence is surjective and reflects zero, which proves surjectivity and equality of kernels.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_affine_open_sections_adic
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) (V : X.affineOpens) :
    let T := F.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)
    (∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite Γ(X, V.1) (T.obj (op n))) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, I.ideal V ^ (n + 1) •
      (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, V.1) (T.obj (op n))) = ⊥) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ∧
      LinearMap.ker (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom =
        I.ideal V ^ (n + 1) •
          (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, V.1) (T.obj (op (n + 1)))))
